blindSummary:
This state/province is the most consistent lethal hotspot for trans and travesti people in the country's worst-affected region: 11 killings in 2024 (3rd nationally, 1st in the region) and 8 in 2025 (tied for the highest state total in the country). Against a population of ~9 million this yields roughly 0.9 killings per million per year — more than double the national rate of ~0.38 per million. The 2025 dossier further notes a concentration of Black victims here.

The elevated exposure is driven by sustained, patterned lethality rather than any legal distinction (national criminal law applies uniformly). Compared with the much larger state that matched this total in 2025, this state/province's smaller population puts its per-capita rate at roughly double the national per-million rate.

For a visibly trans visitor the pattern matters: the killings are concentrated on young Black trans women in public space — precisely the exposure profile of a conspicuous traveller — and consistency across two years signals an entrenched environment rather than a statistical blip.
